original_question: Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?
target_in_paper: Section 4.9, Open Problem 41: the representation question for visibility graphs of simple polygons. The surrounding Section 4 makes clear that the relevant notion of visibility graph here is the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon, and Section 4.3 frames realization as drawing a simple polygon with the given visibility graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core substance of the paper's question: whether a visibility graph can be realized with integer coordinates whose bit-complexity is only polynomial. That is exactly the issue raised in Open Problem 41. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The scope is narrower than 'every visibility graph' in the survey: Open Problem 41 is specifically about visibility graphs of simple polygons, since it appears inside Section 4, 'Visibility graph theory: Polygons.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

A stand-alone version should say that G is assumed to be the visibility graph of some simple polygon, and asks for another realizing simple polygon with the same visibility graph; Section 4.3 defines reconstruction in exactly this sense. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
The ambient coordinate domain should be explicit: the polygon's vertex (equivalently, edge-endpoint) coordinates are required to lie in Z^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The polynomial bound should be quantified in terms of the size of the instance, naturally n = |V(G)| for an n-vertex polygon visibility graph. The paper leaves this dependence implicit, so a fully stand-alone reformulation should make it explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To avoid ambiguity about 'visibility graph,' the question should state the polygon visibility relation: two graph vertices are adjacent iff the segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely within the polygon. This is the notion used in Section 4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The nearby context also notes that some visibility graphs require exponential-size integers, and that a polynomial-bit bound would imply recognition is in NP; this is motivation rather than part of the formal question, but it explains why the bit bound matters. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: Let G be the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon P with n vertices; that is, V(G) corresponds to the vertices of P, and two vertices of G are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely within P. Must there exist some simple polygon P' realizing the same visibility graph G whose vertex coordinates all lie in Z^2 and whose x- and y-coordinates each have bit-length bounded by a polynomial in n? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 41 rather than any of the point-visibility or segment-visibility problems, because the paper's only open question about integer-coordinate realizations with polynomially many bits appears in Section 4.9 on polygon visibility graphs. The main paper-faithful correction is therefore scope: 'every visibility graph' is too broad, while the paper asks this only for visibility graphs of simple polygons. I also made explicit what 'realized' means by using the reconstruction language from Section 4.3, and I exposed the implicit parameter n controlling the polynomial bit bound. The paper further explains that a positive answer would place visibility-graph recognition in NP. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
